catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds an unacknowledged ROS topic publication of a NED Point goal on a world.sim resource. cap.world.step.v1 advances a world by ticks and returns an observation and state_hash; cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 is a planar linear/angular velocity command with duration and distance/heading outputs on robot.mobile_base; cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is a robot.arm inverse-kinematics pose in millimetres. The upstream interface is a geometry_msgs/Point topic subscription, so the package uses an x-cap id with an inline schema.

No catalogue class observes a visualization_msgs/Marker trail on a world.sim resource. cap.sensing.read.v1 requires a sensor, sensor.imu or sensor.force_torque resource and returns sampled_at/sequence; cap.world.step.v1 is an advancing action, not a marker observation. The upstream output is a visualisation LINE_STRIP, so the package uses an x-cap id with an inline schema.
catalogue_requests.summary: Read the last point of the /mavswarm2/robot_3/trajectory marker.

notes:

Last gate run 2026-11-04T23:52:47-08:00, backend fake, exit 1: G1 pass Layout; G2 pass Lock; G3 pass Strict resolve; G4 pass Provenance; G5 pass Reference; G6 fail Behaviour with G6.ESTOP_FAILED: mhs.safety.estop status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED: the device reports that its safe state was not reached; the latch stays engaged; retrying in the background (estop 'engaged', expected engaged or software_only); G7 pass Native surface; G8 pass Protocol and surface; G9 skip G9.NOT_RUN: not run: fix the failing gates first. The report is check-report.json in this directory.

WHY THE HELPER CANNOT CONFIRM A STOP: the pinned clone creates no ROS service or action server for control, reset or stop. A search of include/, src/, launch/ and publish_words.py found no create_service, create_action_server, rclcpp_action, ros::Service or actionlib declaration. The constructor's ROS interfaces are the wall timer, the desired_state subscription and the trajectory publisher (include/mavswarm2/quadrotor.hpp:70-107); desired_pos_cb only accepts a new Point goal (include/mavswarm2/quadrotor.hpp:212-223), and publish_path only publishes the trail (include/mavswarm2/quadrotor.hpp:279-304). main spins and calls rclcpp::shutdown() only after spin returns (src/quadrotor.cpp:23-33); that is a process path, not an acknowledged ROS stop. A desired_state publication near the current target can make the planner hold, but a ROS topic publication has no acknowledgement and the clone reports no measured quiescence. The RosDriver safety_status therefore reports achieved=false for this effectful ROS control surface; the stock e-stop fails and the software latch only fences this driver's publications. An operator must stop the ROS process or publish a hover goal outside the latched driver path. No physical e-stop exists or is claimed.

SCOPE: a configuration-only ROS 2 RosDriver over rosbridge, mode simulated, risk R0, device_kind world.sim; no native.py and no Python native class. The package binds one launched vehicle, robot_3, because the clone's exact absolute endpoint comment is /mavswarm2/robot_3/desired_state (include/mavswarm2/quadrotor.hpp:93) and /mavswarm2/robot_3/trajectory (include/mavswarm2/quadrotor.hpp:105). x-cap.malintha.desired_state.v1 publishes one geometry_msgs/msg/Point goal (NED frame, metres, per publish_words.py:17-19 and 247-248) and returns published=true, confirmed=false only. x-cap.malintha.trajectory.v1 subscribes to the node's visualization_msgs/msg/Marker LINE_STRIP and returns the last point in the marker header frame map; the resource state exposes the trail and last_goal wire observations. NOT COVERED: TF map -> robot_<id>/base_link (the clone uses tf2_ros but declares no /tf subscription), the SCP path and neighbour traffic, the other nine robots, ROS parameters, sensors, camera, RViz, world step, reset, snapshot and restore. This is one vehicle, not a swarm-level orchestration interface.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: fake.py is a ROS-free mhs.bridge.ros_transport RecordingRosTransport contract stand-in, not captured traffic and not the upstream simulator. Engine analytic:ROS contract fake (canned replies; no Mavswarm2 node or physics), level F0, determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none, no snapshot/restore. It answers a placeholder trajectory marker and echoes the last recorded goal on the command topic; every fake number is marked # placeholder. It runs no SCP planner, geometric controller, GSL/Eigen dynamics, TF or RViz and does not apply a goal; the last_goal echo is a disclosed gap because a live volatile command subscription is not a replay of the last goal. The upstream was not built or launched; it needs ROS 2, colcon, GSL/Eigen and the external simulator_interfaces package, and no live ROS graph or hardware run is claimed.

LIMITS, RISK AND TESTS: the clone states no numeric goal envelope. The SCP planner's v_max/a_max are internal solver defaults, the launch initial_conditions and publish_words.py glyph constants are configured layouts, and the callback's 0.2 m deadband is a behaviour threshold. All three goal inputs are Limit.operator_required, so a goal is refused with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies site-limits.json; site-limits.example.json is illustrative example data only. Risk R0 is the card floor: this package binds only simulated state and one simulated vehicle's visualisation, with no physical equipment. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds eight simulator cases (trajectory observation, desired_state publication wire shape, operator-limit refusal, resource trail and last_goal, last_goal change, silent and malformed trajectory failures, the unconfirmed e-stop and latch); the eight simulator cases pass, while the gate case is expected to fail G6 for the recorded blocker. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was emitted. The clone is unmodified at f2cc09b22e4752c057cb8cc29c47e6fecfe04dde. No network, pip install or upstream execution was used; driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null and no human reviewed or tested anything. The fake is a contract stand-in only; the check report's evidence_state is none because G6 failed, so no contract-checked, live-simulation or hardware evidence is claimed. The loader refuse [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the pinned mavswarm2 node creates a wall timer, the per-robot desired_state subscription, a TF broadcaster and the trajectory marker publisher and no service or action (quadrotor.hpp:59-125), and main only spins and then shuts down (quadrotor.cpp:23-33), so no acknowledged stop exists and the stock e-stop fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the latch held (HELPER_MISSING for a simulator). The endpoints (relative robot_3/... names under the mavswarm2 namespace of quadrotor.launch:42-47), the Point and Marker types, the operator_required NED goal bounds with their example overlay, the ROS 2 stamp fields of the fake and all 20 facts were checked. Defects: two facts said more than their lines (the dt log on line 68 outside 70-72; a TF broadcast described from the broadcaster's construction lines), the licence split was not recorded, and the last_goal resource read subscribes to the desired_state command topic that only clients publish: a reviewer probe with that topic silent showed each command waiting the 2 s read timeout and mhs.resource.read failing MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY, which the fake hides by answering at once; removing the read made the gate also fail TCAP-003 (no observable effect), so the read stays and is disclosed. Reviewer changed driver.py (two facts corrected, three licence facts, one fidelity gap, a comment on the last_goal read) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate still fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the stable digest unchanged, and the eight package cases pass. For the human reviewer: Simulation only: each Quadrotor node integrates its own dynamics on a wall timer with no pause, reset or stop service. Whoever unblocks it must replace the last_goal read of the command topic with real feedback, since in a live graph it makes every command wait 2 s and mhs.resource.read fail NOT_READY. publish_words.py publishes goals to all ten robots and competes with this driver; launch/simu.launch is a stale ROS 1 launch for another package name. Upstream frames are inconsistent: desired_pos_cb compares the NED goal with a target_pos initialised in NWU (quadrotor.hpp:91, 218).
